text.title: Post Migration Cleanup Decision Tree
text.summary: Routing tree mapping observable migration signals (legacy write traffic, legacy read traffic, flag keys, snapshot presence) to a rule from `content/01-core-rules.xml`. Every leaf names a concrete rule id, `run-the-checklist`, or `skip-this-methodology` when cleanup is premature.

decision-tree.root-question: Has 100% of production traffic been served by the new path for at least one full weekly traffic cycle?

conclusion.verdict: skip-this-methodology: the migration is not finished; cleanup before cutover deletes the rollback path

branch.question: Do write metrics on the legacy store still show non-zero traffic, or is the legacy write path still present in code?

conclusion.verdict: run the reconciliation over 7 consecutive days; on zero mismatches delete the legacy write path in its own PR and cite the report

branch.question: Does the legacy read-path counter read zero for a full cycle, and is every migration flag key already deleted from code and the flag service?

conclusion.verdict: identify the remaining callers from the counter; do not delete the read path until it reads zero for 7 days including the batch window
delete each flag key and collapse its branches in one PR per key; record the PR URL against the key

branch.question: Is there a dated snapshot of the legacy data and a zero-hit reference scan before any DROP?

conclusion.verdict: take the snapshot, run the cross-repo and query-log scan, record both; only then schedule the DROP as a separate change
run the full checklist: shims with expiry, docs and runbooks, alerts and infra decommission, cleanup deadline with per-item owners

text.example: Observable: cutover 2026-04-01, legacy write path deleted in PR #8812 after reconciliation showed 0 mismatches over 2026-04-03..2026-04-10; legacy read counter `orders_v1_reads_total` = 0 for 9 days; 3 flag keys deleted → snapshot `s3://backups/orders_v1-2026-04-12` with retention to 2026-10-01, reference scan 0 hits → conclusion: run-the-checklist.
